by_producer.producer: lib/opal_lgctfm.py:374-380 parse_aws_walk() -- comp-find --corpus aws's own S3Key band prints no arn_or_path detail line, so the parser falls back to `name` (bare key, no bucket); reached via discover_involved()'s resolve() (lib/opal_lgctfm.py:956-964) when the (node_type,name) pair is AMBIGUOUS across more than one firm-writer node in the served graph, so by_tn's single-candidate test fails and the row is built from the comp-find-parsed node instead of a kuzu-native one
by_producer.how_it_was_attributed: RAN `.tools/comp-find --corpus aws <bare-key>` for each row's key (e.g. 'advisor_fee_efficiency'): every one returns exactly THREE S3Key candidate nodes with the same name -- opal-data-bd/<key> and opal-data-inf/<key> (props.attribution='writer-firm'), plus a THIRD node keyed 's3:<key>' with empty arn. RAN `.tools/comp-kuzu` Cypher MATCH queries (`MATCH (x:CloudNode) WHERE x.node_type='S3Key' AND x.name='<key>' RETURN x.node_id, x.props`) confirming that third node's props for all 23 rows: source='portal-stitch', origin='stitch', origin_reason='ambiguous-across-firms', n.arn=''. READ lib/opal_lgctfm.py:350-406 (parse_aws_walk/run_aws_walk) -- the function's own docstring states arn_or_path is 'blank for some types, e.g. S3Key', and its code (line 374-380) falls back to `name` when the line after the entry header is blank, which is exactly what comp-find prints for an S3Key hit. READ discover_involved()/resolve() (lib/opal_lgctfm.py:908-964): with 3 same-name candidates, `by_tn.get((node_type,name))` returns len==3 so `nid` stays None and the walk mints a synthetic node from comp-find's own (blank-fallback) output instead of using any of the 3 kuzu-native nodes directly. This is a code-path trace confirmed by live re-runs of the two instruments the engine itself calls, not an inference from the path's own shape.

by_producer.producer: lib/opal_lgctfm.py:929-930 (discover_involved()'s kuzu_rows() ingestion loop) -- `"arn_or_path": r.get("arn") or nid` falls back to the kuzu-native node_id itself when the served graph's own `arn` property is empty
by_producer.how_it_was_attributed: RAN `.tools/comp-kuzu` MATCH for the row's key ('blackdiamond/49f/_ops/pull_state.json'): exactly ONE candidate node, node_id 's3:blackdiamond/49f/_ops/pull_state.json', n.arn='', props.source='portal-stitch', props.origin_reason='no-canonical-s3-key' (a DIFFERENT reason than the 23 ambiguous rows above -- this key is not duplicated across firms, it simply has no canonical S3 key resolved). Because there is exactly ONE candidate (not 3), discover_involved()'s resolve() (lib/opal_lgctfm.py:956-964) matches it directly via by_tn and never falls through to the comp-find-parsed path used by producer 1 -- the row is built straight from the kuzu-native `nodes` dict entry (lib/opal_lgctfm.py:923-930), where `r.get('arn') or nid` falls back to the node_id string itself, which is why this row's value carries the 's3:' prefix (baked into the node_id by whatever upstream process minted it) while the 23 ambiguous rows above carry no prefix at all. Confirmed by a live comp-kuzu re-query, not inferred from the value's shape.
